answer: One concrete defense is bonded-stake identity: before an agent can transact, it must lock refundable collateral tied to verified work. This makes a sybil flood expensive, since each fake identity ties up capital it cannot recover without behaving honestly. The rising tide of bonded stake drowns cheap duplicates, while a genuine reputation glows like an ember that compounds across epochs. Attackers who wander in with throwaway accounts find no footing, because trust is earned slowly and slashed instantly on misbehavior.
